pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #1
====

GRADE: Grade 3
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Attentive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. going
   D. went

3. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only a joining word
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only an action

4. When practising Language Activities at home, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Language Activities at home.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Activities at home.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Language Activities at home.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Language Activities at home.

5. When practising Spelling, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Spelling.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Spelling.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Spelling.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Spelling.

6. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.

7. When practising Punctuation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Punctuation.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Punctuation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Punctuation.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Punctuation.

8. When practising Guided Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Guided Writing.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Guided Writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Guided Writing.

9. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.

10. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. where is the library

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

12. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. run
   B. blue
   C. happiness
   D. quickly

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Spelling and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening.

2. D — went

3. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language Activities at home.

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Spelling.

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Punctuation.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Guided Writing.

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

10. C — Where is the library?

11. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

12. A — run

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Spelling; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Punctuation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Guided Writing; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Attentive Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
